steps.headline: Which speed feels right for the strip?
steps.risk: Every pane has the same mechanics — a peek stays open through a click, the badge opens after the name, a dragged pill rides under your cursor. Only speed and curve differ.

variants.label: Settled
variants.summary: Decelerates fast and stops dead: 150ms hover, 200ms name reveal. What ships if nothing is picked.

variants.label: Crisp
variants.summary: Same curve, a third quicker: 100ms hover, 140ms reveal. Nearly instant, still not a cut.

variants.label: Soft
variants.summary: A plain ease and a little longer: 180ms hover, 260ms reveal. Calmer; you can see the row move.

steps.headline: Does dragging feel like a Chrome tab now?
steps.changed: The pill you grab follows your cursor exactly along the row and never leaves it. The pills it passes step aside one at a time, so the gap is already open where it will land. When you let go it glides the last few pixels into place. Pulling a pill down past the strip still tears it out into its own window.
steps.notice: No more hopping from slot to slot behind the cursor, no spring back to where it started, and no void opening beside a dot you picked up while its name was showing.
steps.risk: A wide pill among dots moves several dots at once as it passes them — that is the row keeping the same total width, not a bug.

steps.headline: How should the conversation arrive?
steps.risk: The conversation you are leaving is never animated. One element moves, so a very long conversation costs no more than a short one.

variants.label: Fade and lift
variants.summary: The conversation fades in while rising 6px, over a quarter second.

variants.label: Fade only
variants.summary: The same fade, no movement. Nothing in the transcript shifts.

variants.label: Cut
variants.summary: No animation. The conversation is simply there, the way Chrome switches a tab.
